title: Should the "focus update steps" consider an `input` element's "input activation steps" rather than just its "activation steps"?
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

Step 2.1 of the [focus update steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focus-update-steps) begins with:

> If entry is an [input](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#the-input-element) element, and the [change](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/indices.html#event-change) event [applies](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#concept-input-apply) to the element, and the element does not have a defined [activation behavior](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#eventtarget-activation-behavior), ...

Unless I'm mistaken, every `input` element has an activation behavior, described here:
https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#the-input-element:activation-behaviour

> The [activation behavior](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#eventtarget-activation-behavior) for [input](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#the-input-element) elements element, given event, are these steps ...

However, not every element has an *input* activation behavior. For example, in the button state, "[The element has no input activation behavior.](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#button-state-(type=button))".

Should the focus update steps be referring to the input activation behavior here?
